description: Start each warning or caution with a clear command, then give the risk in a short explanation.

questions.prompt: When do you use a WARNING instead of a CAUTION?
options: When there is a risk of damage to equipment
When there is a risk of injury or death
questions.explanation: A warning tells the reader about a risk of injury or death. A caution tells the reader about a risk of damage to equipment.

questions.prompt: How must an STE warning start?
options: With the risk, for example 'High voltage can kill.'
With a simple and clear command
questions.explanation: Start a warning or a caution with a simple and clear command. Then give a short explanation of the risk.

questions.prompt: Build the command that starts this warning about hot engine parts:
questions.explanation: Start with a direct command. 'Do not touch the engine until it is cool' is clearer than a polite request such as 'Please avoid touching'.

questions.prompt: Which is the best STE caution?
options: CAUTION: Damage to the seal can occur if the tool is used incorrectly.
CAUTION: Use only a plastic tool to remove the seal. A metal tool can cause damage to the seal.
CAUTION: Be careful with the seal.
questions.explanation: The caution starts with a clear command, then a short sentence gives the risk. The other options do not tell the reader what to do.

questions.prompt: Tap the words that make this warning weak and indirect:
questions.sentence: It is recommended that you disconnect the power before you open the panel.
questions.approvedAlternative: Disconnect the power before you open the panel.
questions.explanation: A warning must give a clear command. 'It is recommended that you' hides the instruction and makes it sound optional.

questions.prompt: Rewrite this warning in 20 words or fewer. Start with a command. Keep 'goggles', 'hydraulic' and 'injury':
questions.initialText: WARNING: It is very important that personnel should always remember to wear the approved safety goggles at all times when they are working with the high-pressure hydraulic system because fluid can cause injury to the eyes.
questions.explanation: Give the command first, then the risk: 'Put on safety goggles near the hydraulic system. Hydraulic fluid can cause injury to your eyes.'
